Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office of an SL. The registered office and tax domicile must be a physical premises situated in Spain where actual management, representation, or administrative operations are located. For offshore wind turbine piling activities, a service-based virtual address may be used only as a supplementary correspondence channel, not as the registered office.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the company's provincial registered office, coordinated where applicable through the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) and the CIRCE system administered by the Directorate-General for Industry and Small and Medium Enterprises.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 20-24, 28-32, 58-63, 210-242, and 253-284; Royal Decree 1784/1996, approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and the CIRCE electronic incorporation system.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed with the competent provincial Mercantile Registry, supported by the certified name-clearance certificate and tax identification documentation.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 213 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 in capital, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have additional liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No statutory escrow account is required for an SL; a bank certificate evidencing monetary contributions may be used, although founders may dispense with that certificate and remain jointly liable for the reality of the contributions. Notarial, registry, name-reservation, publication, tax, and professional fees are separate from any official filing-fee estimate.

Funding & unlock path: Before operation, obtain or document the applicable municipal fire-prevention and opening authorization, emergency and self-protection plan under Royal Decree 393/2007 where applicable, and certification of fire-protection systems under Royal Decree 513/2017. Obtain structural, lifting, electrical, pressure-equipment, machinery, and temporary-works inspections required by the technical project and applicable industrial-safety regulations. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, Royal Decree 1627/1997 for construction works, maritime work and diving rules where applicable, worker training, medical surveillance, personal protective equipment, contractor coordination, and port emergency requirements.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 in capital, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have additional liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No statutory escrow account is required for an SL; a bank certificate evidencing monetary contributions may be used, although founders may dispense with that certificate and remain jointly liable for the reality of the contributions. Notarial, registry, name-reservation, publication, tax, and professional fees are separate from any official filing-fee estimate.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and confirms the subscriptions and fully paid contributions for the quotas stated in the deed of incorporation and articles; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address recorded in the deed, with authority delegated to the sole director or managing directors to file changes; (3) [Name] is appointed sole director/managing director, as applicable, accepting office and declaring no legal impediment; (4) [Name] is appointed secretary, if applicable; and (5) the officers are authorized to obtain the NIF, complete Mercantile Registry filings, open bank accounts, and execute all documents necessary for commencement of business.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Ministry for Industry and Tourism, Directorate-General for Industry, together with the competent autonomous-community industrial authority; offshore project authorizations additionally involve the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, the Directorate-General for the Coast and the Sea, the relevant Port Authority, and competent local authorities.

Category: No single universal national operating license applies to all offshore monopile-installation contractors. Depending on the activity, required instruments may include industrial-establishment registration or responsible declaration, municipal opening or activity authorization, port occupation authorization, coastal public-domain concession, maritime-space compatibility authorization, construction authorization, and project-specific administrative authorization for the wind-farm electrical installation under Law 24/2013 and Royal Decree 1955/2000.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/

E-government filing portal

Foreign entities register with the AEAT to obtain a NIF. Submit Form 036 (for non-residents) or equivalent through a tax representative or online if eligible, including corporate documents, proof of legal existence, and Spanish business activity. Processing typically takes 15-30 days.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Foreign entities register with the AEAT to obtain a NIF. Submit Form 036 (for non-residents) or equivalent through a tax representative or online if eligible, including corporate documents, proof of legal existence, and Spanish business activity. Processing typically takes 15-30 days.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box elections; Spain operates a territorial tax system with entity-level taxation for resident companies. Hybrid mismatch provisions under EU ATAD apply for certain structures.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

1,000,000 EUR annual turnover threshold

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

0% VAT applies to goods exported outside the EU and services supplied to non-EU customers. Requires proof that goods/services leave the EU territory and are not consumed in Spain.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Despacho de Exportación)
  • Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
  • Inward Remittance Certificate
  • Proof of delivery outside EU

Mandatory electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) with real-time data transmission to AEAT. Digital stamps and clearance via the integrated platform; non-compliant invoices rejected. API integration required for large taxpayers.

Claims of fraudulent zero-rating lead to VAT reassessment, interest, fines (up to 100% of tax evaded), and potential criminal liability. Retrospective clawback with surcharges for non-compliance.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and applies the EU framework for free movement of capital and payments. There are no general foreign-exchange controls on current-account payments, capital contributions, dividends, or repatriation of investment proceeds. Banks must conduct sanctions, anti-money-laundering, source-of-funds, and payment-purpose checks. Dividend remittances remain subject to distributable-profit, corporate-approval, withholding-tax, and treaty or EU relief requirements. Foreign investment and cross-border transaction reporting may apply; reporting is not, by itself, an exchange-control approval or a restriction on remittance.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or deadline requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Receipts may be retained in permitted foreign-currency accounts. Applicable bank reporting, Banco de España statistical reporting, tax, customs, sanctions, and documentation obligations still apply. Confirm transaction-specific reporting thresholds and filing duties with the bank and Spanish advisers.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); foreign-exchange policy and payment-system rules are also governed by applicable European Union law and, where relevant, the European Central Bank and the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for routine euro payments and eligible foreign-currency services, subject to the provider's geographic coverage, account terms, and risk appetite. An EU-authorized electronic money institution is not a bank, and safeguarded e-money is not equivalent to a bank deposit or necessarily covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme. Do not rely on an EMI as the sole project-finance, escrow, or letter-of-credit provider. Verify authorization, safeguarding arrangements, payment limits, and correspondent-bank access.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident, layered, nominee, or trust ownership; inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.

Root cause: Non-resident, layered, nominee, or trust ownership; inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.

Defense evidence: Current Spanish company registry extract and constitutional documents; complete ownership chart through all intermediate entities to natural-person beneficial owners; UBO register evidence; identity and address documents; corporate registries and good-standing evidence for foreign owners; certified translations, apostilles, or legalizations as requested; board resolutions and authorized-signatory evidence.
Large initial capital payment or project funding inconsistent with the company profile or originating from an unrelated third party.

Root cause: Large initial capital payment or project funding inconsistent with the company profile or originating from an unrelated third party.

Defense evidence: Executed subscription, shareholder-loan, or financing documents; board approvals; bank statements and audited accounts evidencing source of funds; originator and beneficiary account details; payment instructions identifying the legal purpose; group structure and related-party explanation; supporting tax and investment-reporting records where applicable.
Unclear offshore-wind project purpose, unusually large trade payments, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions.

Root cause: Unclear offshore-wind project purpose, unusually large trade payments, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions.

Defense evidence: Project contracts, tender or concession documents, permits and license status, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading or delivery records, counterparty due-diligence results, beneficial-ownership and sanctions screening, payment schedule, and a reconciliation of each payment to the project budget.
Payments involving sanctioned parties, restricted goods, high-risk intermediaries, or inconsistent payment narratives.

Root cause: Payments involving sanctioned parties, restricted goods, high-risk intermediaries, or inconsistent payment narratives.

Defense evidence: Documented sanctions and export-control screening; end-user and end-use statements where relevant; contractual representations; logistics and vessel documentation; approved bank payment purpose and supporting invoice; escalation records and evidence that no restricted person or activity is involved.
Expected turnover, currencies, jurisdictions, or payment volumes differ materially from the onboarding profile.

Root cause: Expected turnover, currencies, jurisdictions, or payment volumes differ materially from the onboarding profile.

Defense evidence: Updated business plan, annual project cash-flow forecast, expected transaction volumes and corridors, customer and supplier schedules, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, tax registrations, and prompt written updates to the bank.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route shareholder equity and documented shareholder loans from an account held in the investor's own name to the Spanish SL's corporate account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Use accurate remitter and beneficiary names, the Spanish company's legal name and IBAN, and a truthful payment reference identifying share capital, share premium, or loan funding. Provide subscription or loan agreements, corporate approvals, source-of-funds evidence, and bank-requested purpose documentation before transfer. Record the transaction in the company's books and complete applicable Spanish foreign-investment or statistical declarations; do not treat a bank payment-purpose label as a substitute for a legally required filing.Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA and SWIFT cross-border payment instructions for other currencies or destinations; banks may process SWIFT messages under ISO 20022 rather than legacy MT103 formatting. Match each payment to the executed contract, invoice, purchase order, shipping or milestone evidence, and the agreed beneficiary account. For material equipment or construction procurement, request an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit subject to agreed UCP 600 terms, with presentation requirements, expiry, shipment or milestone conditions, and discrepancy procedures settled before issuance. Consider documentary collections or bank guarantees where commercially suitable. Reconcile fees, exchange rates, value dates, and beneficiary receipts.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or eligible investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposure and subject to suitability, collateral, and reporting requirements.Foreign-exchange swaps for documented short-term liquidity or currency-management needs, subject to counterparty limits and applicable EMIR, MiFID II, and bank documentation requirements.Non-deliverable forwards only where legally and commercially available for the relevant currency pair; settlement and counterparty terms must be reviewed because NDFs are not a substitute for a prohibited or unavailable currency conversion.Currency options or cross-currency swaps may be considered for documented project exposures, subject to product eligibility, valuation, collateral, accounting, and applicable derivatives reporting obligations.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for routine euro payments and eligible foreign-currency services, subject to the provider's geographic coverage, account terms, and risk appetite. An EU-authorized electronic money institution is not a bank, and safeguarded e-money is not equivalent to a bank deposit or necessarily covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme. Do not rely on an EMI as the sole project-finance, escrow, or letter-of-credit provider. Verify authorization, safeguarding arrangements, payment limits, and correspondent-bank access.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) applicable to Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

24% for dividends paid to non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment under the general Non-Resident Income Tax rate; 19% for residents of an EU/EEA state with effective exchange of tax information; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 5% of the Spanish SL, and potentially 0-15% under a bilateral tax treaty (DTA).

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

For a fiscal year closed on 31 December, the annual Modelo 200 return must be filed and paid by 25 July of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the filing deadline is the 25th day after the lapse of six months from the fiscal year-end.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 – Entity identification Taxpayer identification (NIF), full legal name, registered address, and fiscal residence declarations; also the Spanish branch data where applicable. For a Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders, enter the SL as the taxable entity. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain do not file Modelo 200; they are subject to Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source income through specific IRNR forms. Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.
Box 2 – Activity classification and territory Primary CNAE activity code and, where applicable, separate line items for construction, installation services, and other income attributable to a permanent establishment or to foreign operations. The Spanish SL must record the CNAE code corresponding to marine construction/offshore wind turbine pilings, e.g. CNAE 4291 / 4390. Non-resident shareholders should not be shown as taxpayers unless they have a Spanish permanent establishment through which the wind piling activity is economically carried out. Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.
Box 3 – Accounting result and adjustments Start from the accounting net profit/loss, then apply all extra-accounting adjustments (permanent and temporary differences, depreciation/amortisation, provisions, impairment losses, and tax-exempt income). Prepared from the Spanish statutory financial statements of the SL. Transactions with non-resident related parties must be adjusted for transfer pricing differences using arm’s length values; the corresponding adjustments are shown in the reconciliation to taxable base. Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.
Box 4 – Taxable base and tax losses Resulting taxable income after integrating current-year adjustments and offsetting prior-year negative tax bases, showing any utilisation of available tax loss carryforwards. Only the SpanishSL’s taxable base is declared. Non-resident shareholders cannot offset losses of the Spanish SL against their own foreign-source income, and any dividend distribution to non-residents is subject to withholding at the time the profits are deemed distributed. Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.
Box 5 – Total tax, credits, and payments Final gross tax due, application of tax credits (including double-taxation relief and R&D credits), withheld taxes, quarterly instalments, and the resulting amount to pay or to request for refund. Foreign tax credits for tax paid by the SL in other jurisdictions are computed in this SL. Withholding taxes on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents are not calculated on Modelo 200 but are declared by the paying entity through the quarterly withholding declarations (Modelo 216/123) and annual returns. Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 (aggregate related-party transactions threshold for the Spanish Local File); Master File is required when the ultimate parent’s consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 45,000,000; Country-by-Country Report is required for groups with consolidated revenue equal to or above EUR 750,000,000.

Economic substance scope: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute exists in Spain; however, economic substance is an operational requirement through the general anti-abuse clause (Art. 15 LGT), simulation/nullity rules, CFC rules, anti-hybrid rules, and the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI. A Spanish SL engaged in offshore wind turbine piling must demonstrate actual operational substance (office/premises, qualified employees, project management, engineering/installation decision-making, financing and risk assumption). If the SL is a conduit with no real activity, the tax authority may deny treaty benefits and recharacterize the flow as a sham distribution subject to penalties and possible criminal charges.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)

Statutory sanction: Criminal: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus a proportional fine of 2 to 6 times the defrauded tax amount where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000; aggravated if the amount exceeds EUR 600,000 or international tax fraud is proven, with imprisonment increased to 2 to 6 years and fines of 6 to 12 times the defrauded amount. Administrative: proportional penalty of 50%-100% of the missing amount, increased to 100%-150% in cases of obstruction or material dissimulation of facts.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax debts and penalty surcharges if they caused or induced the valuation/manipulation; in criminal proceedings, the court may impose personal imprisonment, travel bans, asset embargoes, and disqualification from managing public or corporate funds.
Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement / Sham Structure

Statutory sanction: Spanish tax authorities may disregard the arrangement under the general anti-abuse rule (Art. 15 LGT), apply the arm’s length principle to re-attribute income, deny treaty relief under the MLI Principal Purpose Test, and assess back taxes plus late-payment interest and penalties of 50%-100% of the adjusted amount; the entity may additionally be re-qualified as having a permanent establishment in Spain for the non-resident parent.

Director personal liability: Directors and formal shareholders may be held personally liable for the re-assessed tax and penalties if they knowingly participated in the artificial scheme; in severe cases, the criminal tax evasion threshold can be reached, leading to imprisonment, travel restrictions, and disqualification orders.
Money Laundering / AML Compliance Breach

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines for serious and very serious AML offences under Spanish Law 10/2010 range from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 depending on the type and persistence of the violation (very serious infractions can reach the greater of EUR 150,001 or 2% of the offending institution’s resources). Criminal money laundering (Art. 301 Penal Code) can impose imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years and fines; assets and profits connected to the offence are confiscated.

Director personal liability: Directors, beneficial owners, and compliance officers can face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and individual fines; courts may order preventive embargoes of personal and corporate assets and travel bans during the investigation; directors who fail to maintain an adequate AML prevention system in the SL are personally exposed to administrative fines and civil damages.
Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Arm’s-Length Misstatement

Statutory sanction: Failure to provide required TP documentation triggers administrative penalties per Art. 186 LGT: between EUR 1,000 and EUR 15,000 per incident/document depending on the type and completeness of the documentation, and the AEAT can re-assess the taxable base at arm’s length with late-payment interest and a 50%-100% proportional penalty on the additional tax; if the correction results in a tax shortfall exceeding EUR 120,000 and is intentional, criminal tax evasion risk materialises.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign false or incomplete TP documentation, knowingly approve unfair intercompany prices, or fail to implement the required transfer pricing controls can be held personal civil partners of the corporate penalty; in criminal cases, the director can be imprisoned and disqualified from acting as a legal representative or administer third-party assets.
